Notes

Yoyi turns low expectations into swagger, User116 chooses everyday pleasure, and Jackzebra sends the whole contact list into a comic void.

要钱没有烂命一条

要钱没有，要命一条 is a defiant formula: there is no money to hand over, only one life. Replacing the second demand with 烂命, “rotten life,” devalues even that last possession. Yoyi then says this supposedly worthless life is going extremely well. The opening is less surrender than a way of making himself impossible to threaten: what can you take from someone who mocks his own price?

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
当面一套背后一套

当面 and 背后 oppose being in front of somebody with being behind their back. 一套 names an entire way of behaving, not one isolated lie. The speaker claims to recognize both versions. It sets up the sarcastic politeness that follows: smiling, calling someone darling and inviting bigger promises can themselves become a second face.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
说为我好

为我好 is the familiar justification that advice or interference is being offered for somebody’s benefit. The response is only a smile. Once empty promises follow, that smile reads as recognition rather than agreement. Yoyi does not rebut each claim; he lets apparently caring language reveal its usefulness to the person speaking it.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
饼画大点再大点

画饼 is drawing food instead of supplying it: an attractive promise that never becomes something usable. Its older form, 画饼充饥, means trying to satisfy hunger with a picture. Yoyi makes the metaphor literal by demanding a bigger pie because he is still hungry. The affectionate 宝子, “darling,” and dry 呵呵 laughter make the encouragement sarcastic. He exposes the offer without ending the performance, inviting the promiser to continue digging.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 畫餅充饑
那我缅怀

缅怀 is elevated, commemorative language for remembering someone or something with feeling. Answering the question about dead culture with this word gives the complaint a mock funeral. It sits in a line crowded with English profanity and copycat accusations, so the dignified register lasts only a moment before the competitive banter resumes.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
屌

屌 begins as a vulgar anatomical word but also works as slang for formidable or impressively good. Here it is a style boast, strengthened by English “swag” and the refusal to be cloned. The following 烂命太好 turns the earlier “worthless life” inside out: the thing supposedly worth nothing is now enviably good. The humor depends on holding both claims.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
给你脸

给脸 offers somebody face—respect or a chance to retain dignity. Saying they reject it is a reprimand, not a generous offer still open for negotiation. User116 pairs it with an offer of money, so both material and social credit have been refused. The repeated 给……不要 construction makes the other person sound determined to waste every way of being treated well.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
按时睡觉

User116 changes direction abruptly: the confrontation gives way to small instructions for getting through a day. Regular sleep, smiling and staying in the present are ordinary, almost rehearsed reassurances. The following admission that it will still hurt prevents the sequence from becoming effortless optimism. The verse wants improvement while allowing that repeated advice does not instantly deliver it.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
钱不钱的无所谓

Repeating a noun around 不—钱不钱的—loosely dismisses the whole question of money. But the next line says what matters is using it properly, and soon he happily admits greed. The contradiction is conversational, not a formal economic position: money can be something he refuses to worship and something he still wants.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
好看的加满我的微信

好吃的 and 好看的 use matching grammar: tasty things for the stomach, good-looking people for the contact list. The missing nouns let desire classify both as things he wants more of. He then chooses a good-looking feed background too. That small sequence turns taste, attraction and self-presentation into one parallel set of everyday appetites.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
朋友圈

朋友圈 literally means “circle of friends” and is WeChat’s Moments feed. A background image is part of how that small public self appears to contacts. Here it belongs beside food and attractive people as an ordinary pleasure. When Jackzebra later opens the same feed to announce universal death, the platform connects the verses: the location stays the same, but its mood collapses.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
俗人贪财好色

俗人 places him among ordinary, worldly people rather than above material desire. 贪财好色 openly embraces two conventionally disapproved appetites, money and sex. After the routine of sleep, smiles and good food, the line refuses an elevated moral program. Wanting modest enjoyment and admitting unflattering desires become parts of the same decision to stay alive on human terms.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
平均半小时一首歌

The production boast arrives after “let’s just mess around” and before recording whenever the mood takes him. It presents speed as a kind of freedom: making songs need not involve permission, ceremony or a grand statement. The computer and late-night voice give this philosophy an ordinary setting. The half-hour figure is the verse’s boast, not a stopwatch measurement.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
鬼哭狼嚎

鬼哭狼嚎 literally means ghosts crying and wolves howling, a set expression for awful wailing. Jackzebra applies it to his own recording immediately after calling music easy. That self-insult keeps the confidence comic. He gets to make noise on his own terms while anticipating exactly the complaint a tired neighbor might make about it.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
又一幺幺六杰泽比

This phonetic roll call names the three credited performers: Yoyi, User116 and Jackzebra. 幺 is the spoken digit one, often used to distinguish it clearly when reading a number. Turning their names into 又一幺幺六杰泽比 makes the group sound like one continuous chant, briefly converting a set of separate verses into a shared signature.

  • jackzebra: official feature credits
我微信222个人全部都死了

The oddly exact 222 makes the announcement sound like an inventory of actual contacts, then the claim swallows the announcer too. User116 has just filled WeChat with attractive people and valued staying alive; Jackzebra deletes the whole social world in words. It is an escalating performance of dismissal, staged on the very platform that keeps the people connected.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
我们死了

The announcement moves through I, you, we and you-all before arriving at everybody. This is a deliberately exhaustive roll call, not just repetition of a punchline. Every grammatical place from which somebody could answer is folded into the joke. The final return to 命 then has a cleared stage: no particular person gets to escape it.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
这就是命

命 has carried a life that can be offered up, judged worthless or enjoyed; here it becomes fate. English needs a new word, but Chinese lets the same syllable turn existence into a verdict. 不得不, “have no choice but to,” then insists on belief and acceptance. “Never Give Up” later reopens precisely this question by asking whether he must 认命.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
